---
title: "Lab 05 — Estimation, uncertainty, and hypothesis testing"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
survey <- read_csv("data/survey_attitudes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
two <- survey |> filter(education %in% c("Bachelor", "Postgraduate"))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab05", title = "Estimation and hypothesis testing")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A 95% confidence interval means…",
  q2 = "A p-value is…",
  q3 = "Bachelor vs postgraduate mean support in this survey…",
  q4 = "A tiny, very precise difference can be statistically detectable and still unimportant. Give one IR example."
)
```

## What you will do

Read an interval and a test as uncertainty, not as proof of a policy. Download the `.txt`.

`t.test` subtracts in alphabetical order: Bachelor minus Postgraduate. A negative interval means postgraduates score higher.

```{r test-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
two |>
  group_by(education) |>
  summarise(mean_support = mean(support_international_cooperation), .groups = "drop")
t.test(support_international_cooperation ~ education, data = two)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("About 95% of such intervals, built the same way, would cover the population parameter.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The parameter has a 95% chance of sitting in this one already-computed interval."),
  answer("95% of the respondents agree."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The probability, if the null were true, of a result at least this extreme.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The probability that the null hypothesis is true."),
  answer("The size of the effect."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Postgraduate respondents score higher on average (about 5.7 vs 5.2). That is a description of this sample, not a causal effect of education.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The test proves that postgraduate study causes support for cooperation."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(lab_prompts[["q4"]], open_answer(), trim = TRUE)
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
